title: Minimum Cost to Make Two Binary Strings Equal
summary: Given two binary strings s and t , both of length n , and three positive integers flipCost , swapCost , and crossCost , determine the minimum total cost required to make s and t identical.
statement: Given two binary strings s and t , both of length n , and three positive integers flipCost , swapCost , and crossCost , determine the minimum total cost required to make s and t identical. You can apply the following operations any number of times in any order: - Choose any index i and flip s[i] or t[i] (change '0' to '1' or '1' to '0'). The cost of this operation is flipCost . - Choose two distinct indices i and j , and swap either s[i] and s[j] or t[i] and t[j] . The cost of this operation is swapCost . - Choose an index i and swap s[i] with t[i] . The cost of this operation is crossCost . Return the minimum total cost needed to make the strings s and t equal.
constraints: s and t are equal-length binary strings of length up to 100,000.
A flip changes one bit; a swap exchanges two positions within one string; a cross swap exchanges s[i] and t[i].
All costs are positive; return the minimum cost to make the strings equal.
reference_solution:
def minimum_binary_strings_equal_cost(s,t,flip_cost,swap_cost,cross_cost):
    counts=[0,0]
    for left,right in zip(s,t):
        if left!=right:counts[int(left)]+=1
    low=min(counts);high=max(counts);answer=(low+high)*flip_cost
    answer=min(answer,low*swap_cost+(high-low)*flip_cost)
    paired=(low+high)//2
    answer=min(answer,(paired-low)*cross_cost+paired*swap_cost+(low+high-2*paired)*flip_cost)
    return answer

hints: Mismatches have two types: s=0,t=1 or s=1,t=0; positions within a type are otherwise interchangeable.
A normal swap fixes one mismatch of each type, while a cross swap converts one type into the other and a flip fixes one mismatch.
Compare all flips, pair opposite types then flip excess, and cross-convert enough excess to maximize swap pairs.
Any operation sequence reduces to counts of these three actions; within each linear region the cheapest count occurs at one of these boundary plans.

tests.explanation: Pairing opposite mismatch types with swaps, converting a pair with a cross swap, and flipping the leftover costs sixteen.
Three independent flips cost six and beat either swap operation.
